simple.meaning: אֲפֵלָה (ʼăphêlâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “duskiness , figuratively, misfortune ; concrete, concealment.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 10:22. The surrounding context includes land, Egypt.

simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

timeline.evidenceText: Moses stretched out his hand toward the sky, and there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt for three days.
You will grope at noonday, as the blind gropes in darkness, and you shall not prosper in your ways. You will only be oppressed and robbed always, and there will be no one to save you.
The way of the wicked is like darkness.
in the twilight, in the evening of the day,
and look to the earth, and see distress, darkness, and the gloom of anguish. They will be driven into thick darkness.
and if you pour out your soul to the hungry,
Therefore justice is far from us,
Therefore their way will be to them as slippery places in the darkness.
A day of darkness and gloominess,
That day is a day of wrath, a day of distress and anguish, a day of trouble and ruin, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and blackness,
